phase6_exposure.gate9_reading: The gap is 25.57pp, far outside the 10pp band, so gate 9 can only pass on the second limb: the gap is fully attributed. phase8_multiple_testing.note: The naive product overstates the search: most combinations were never run, and E14 reported every cell of its 7x4 grid rather than selecting from it, which is the opposite of p-hacking.
phase8_multiple_testing.reading: Multiple testing is NOT the binding problem here, and saying so is more useful than invoking it. The declared h=20 result has a nominal two-sided p of 0.22 -- it is not significant before any correction, so no correction can change the conclusion. The h=1 result (t = 8.78) survives Bonferroni by a wide margin and is nonetheless worthless, because E14 showed it is a price-limit queue artifact. The programme's problem was never that it found a false positive by searching too hard; it is that the one overwhelming statistical result it found is untradeable, and the one tradable horizon has no result at all.
